focus: TUBAD_RootTangle converted from Mineable to an impassable never-growing Plant (XML + Growth=1 at spawn), and DungeonSite.Draw override rotating the zoomed-in world icon by -90 degrees
diffSource: since build 25 (2026-10-09T23:53:49Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Root tangle no longer hides the chamber behind it: fog floods through and sight passes it
findings.detail: The fog flood stops only at an edifice whose def.MakeFog is true (FloodFillerFog.PassCheck). Line of sight uses GridsUtility.Filled, which also checks only the edifice. A Plant is never an edifice, so fillPercent 1 has no effect on either. When GenStep_Fog floods out from PlayerStartSpot, it now passes through every root-tangle squeeze and unfogs the cavern behind it at generation. The rubble, ice and sand plugs (still Mineable) keep their chambers hidden, so the dungeon is now inconsistent. Decide whether this is acceptable. If it is not, the root tangle has to be an edifice again (a Building thingClass). That gives up the vanilla chop-wood designator, which is the trade-off to weigh. At minimum, update the comment on TUBAD_PlugBase so the tangle is not described as hiding the next chamber.

findings.title: harvestTag Wood makes the tangle a tree, so tree-lover penalties fire when it is chopped
findings.detail: PlantProperties.IsTree is keyed off harvestTag, and treeLoversCareIfChopped defaults to true. With Ideology active, chopping a root tangle records a HistoryEventDefOf.CutTree event and calls treeDestructionTracker.Notify_TreeCut (Plant.PlantCollected). Designator_PlantsHarvestWood also shows the tree-lover warning. Clearing dungeon plugs would then upset tree-loving colonists. Add <treeLoversCareIfChopped>false</treeLoversCareIfChopped> to the <plant> block of TUBAD_RootTangle.

findings.title: New static MaterialPropertyBlock on DungeonSite without [StaticConstructorOnStartup]
findings.detail: StaticConstructorOnStartupUtility.ReportProbablyMissingAttributes logs a warning for any type that holds a MaterialPropertyBlock field and lacks the attribute. The DungeonSite class declaration (DungeonSite.cs:15) shows none. Vanilla WorldObject keeps the same kind of field (WorldObject.cs:41). I ran out of tool calls before confirming exactly when the check runs, so the warning is likely rather than certain. Add [StaticConstructorOnStartup] to DungeonSite, as WorldDrawLayer_Dungeons already does at line 16.

findings.title: Saves with an open dungeon map hold root tangles saved as Mineable
findings.detail: Map things are saved with their runtime class. If anyone has a save with a party inside a dungeon from build 25 or earlier, its root tangles would probably reload as Mineable instances on what is now a Plant-category def. I did not confirm the scribe behaviour or whether any release has shipped (build_history found no v1.0.0 tag). This only matters if those saves exist.
